title: VelocityNote — Markdown notes at the speed of thought
excerpt: A cross-platform, local-first Markdown notebook with cloud sync — and AI that runs entirely on your own machine.
content_html:
A cross-platform, local-first Markdown notebook with cloud sync — and AI that runs entirely on your own machine.

VelocityNote

The demo has not been built for this deployment.
Run dropnote-server/build-landing.sh before deploying.

MCP & agent skills Local AI models Cloud Sync

Small footprint. Full notebook.

A native app under 100 MB — including the full-text retrieval AI agents need and local AI execution runtimes — built to keep memory pressure low, open quickly, and search complete vaults locally.

  • Low install size and low memory pressure
  • SQLite FTS5 searches every note for you and connected AI agents
  • Markdown, diagrams, math, attachments, voice, import, and agent tools are built in
  • Execute local AI models with llama.cpp and ONNX runtimes built in

Your notes, ready for your AI tools.

Connect an AI assistant once, then ask it to find, draft, organize, and link notes in your vault. Its changes appear as normal Markdown notes you can review and edit.

  • Searches titles, tags, links, and full text
  • Creates the tables, tasks, math, and diagrams the app already supports
  • Links related notes instead of copying the same context into every answer
  • Everything it writes remains an ordinary note, tagged ai_notes, and yours to edit

Why VelocityNote

VelocityNote is designed around four things: speed, useful AI access, features that work together, and notes you continue to own.

Your AI tools work with the same notes you do

Connect an AI assistant directly to your vault. It can search, read, write, organize, and link notes, while every result remains ordinary Markdown you can edit.

Search stays fast as your notebook grows

Full-text search is built into the vault, so results appear as you type and are ready as soon as the app opens.

The essentials work together

Tables, tasks, footnotes, math, diagrams, wiki links, voice transcription, import, and search are built in and designed to work as one product.

The notes stay yours

Your notes are Markdown on a computer you control, and the app opens them without a network connection. Export gives you the same .md files, with images beside them, whenever you want them.

Fast local notes, reliable Markdown, and AI help when you want it.

Connect your agent

VelocityNote is the MCP server — nothing extra to install, no service to keep running. Preferences prints the line; paste it and restart your agent.

  1. Open Preferences → MCP and turn on Allow agent access
  2. Press Copy command — the address and the token are already in it
  3. Paste it into your terminal and restart your agent
  4. The tools appear under /mcp: search, read, create, patch, tag, file

Other clients (Cursor, Claude Desktop, your own script) get the same thing as JSON. The endpoint is on loopback and refuses anything without the token.

Ask your own notes

Your assistant can search the vault when a task depends on your past work. Results name the notes used so you can check them.

  1. Connect your assistant once in Preferences
  2. Ask in plain words — no syntax, no note ids
  3. It searches the vault, then reads only the notes that matched
  4. Answers name the notes they came from.

VelocityNote searches full text, titles, tags, and links, then shows which notes supported the answer.

Bring the right context

Say what you are working on and how many tokens you can spare. get_context returns one markdown bundle — the right notes, trimmed to fit, with their sources.

  1. Call get_context with the task and a token budget
  2. It picks by full-text match, tags, [[wiki]] links and recency
  3. You get markdown, its sources, and an estimated token count
  4. Follow the graph from there: get_backlinks, get_links, get_outline

The context lives in your vault, not in one chat history — so the next session starts where the last one left off.

Import all your notes within minutes

Two paths, and which one you take depends only on what you already have. Both show you a preview first — nothing is written until you approve it.

Already Markdown? Do it yourself

  1. Open Preferences → Import, choose Markdown folder or Obsidian vault
  2. Pick the folder and the notebook it lands in
  3. Read the plan — nothing is written yet — then press Import

Anything else? The agent converts it

  1. Point your agent at the folder or the export file
  2. It converts to Markdown — original dates, images and folders survive
  3. It runs import_folder as a dry run and shows you the count
  4. You say yes. Re-runs update those notes instead of duplicating them

Notion, Word, PDF, Evernote and the rest are converted into the same Markdown folder format the app reads natively — one importer, one format, no second path.

content_html_zh:
A cross-platform, local-first Markdown notebook with cloud sync — and AI that runs entirely on your own machine.

VelocityNote

The demo has not been built for this deployment. Run dropnote-server/build-landing.sh before deploying.

MCP & agent skills Local AI models Cloud Sync

Small footprint. Full notebook.

A native app under 100 MB — including the full-text retrieval AI agents need and local AI execution runtimes — built to keep memory pressure low, open quickly, and search complete vaults locally.

  • Low install size and low memory pressure
  • SQLite FTS5 searches every note for you and connected AI agents
  • Markdown, diagrams, math, attachments, voice, import, and agent tools are built in
  • Execute local AI models with llama.cpp and ONNX runtimes built in

VelocityNote is the MCP server — nothing extra to install, no service to keep running. Preferences prints the line; paste it and restart your agent.

  1. Open Preferences → MCP and turn on Allow agent access
  2. Press Copy command — the address and the token are already in it
  3. Paste it into your terminal and restart your agent
  4. The tools appear under /mcp: search, read, create, patch, tag, file

Other clients (Cursor, Claude Desktop, your own script) get the same thing as JSON. The endpoint is on loopback and refuses anything without the token.
